title: Normal restore point mistaken for a rollback guarantee
expected_feedback: Critical: the restore point is not the safety net the comment claims. Without GUARANTEE FLASHBACK DATABASE this is a *normal* restore point — an alias for an SCN, not a promise that you can get back to it. Whether the flashback succeeds depends on the required flashback logs still existing, which is bounded by DB_FLASHBACK_RETENTION_TARGET, and Oracle documents that as a target rather than a guarantee; the restore point itself also ages out of the control file without anyone dropping it. So the column drop, which auto-commits and cannot be crossed by FLASHBACK TABLE, still has no recovery path. Either add GUARANTEE FLASHBACK DATABASE — which does enforce log retention, needs ARCHIVELOG plus FRA space, and must be dropped explicitly at sign-off or it fills the FRA — or take a keyed copy of the column before the drop. Classify the phase restore/PITR either way.
violated_rule: Irreversible statements need a pre-DDL artefact
